name: Uluwatu
hazards: Shallow coral reef
Strong currents on bigger swells
Cave entry and exit is tide-dependent

sections.name: The Peak
sections.notes: The most accessible take-off zone and the busiest part of the reef.

sections.name: Racetrack
sections.notes: Fast down-the-line wall that runs once the swell has size behind it.

sections.name: Temples
sections.notes: The furthest section down the reef, working on the larger, cleaner days.

sections.name: Outside Corner
sections.notes: Only switches on when the swell is big; long, drawn-out walls.

sections.name: The Bombie
sections.notes: The outermost peak, reserved for the largest swells of the dry season.

notes: The anchor wave of the Bukit Peninsula. Five distinct sections activate at different tides and swell sizes, so the same reef reads as a different wave from one session to the next. At its best across the dry season on established SE trades, with June to August delivering the most powerful swell of the year.

name: Padang Padang
hazards: Very shallow coral reef
Heavy, hollow take-off
The whole line-up concentrates on one peak
notes: The most demanding wave on the Bukit and the shortest-tempered. It needs a bigger swell than the neighbouring breaks before it will start, and it wants the higher tides, so it sits dormant on days when Bingin and Balangan are perfect. When both conditions land together in June to August it is the best barrel on the peninsula.

name: Bingin
hazards: Shallow coral reef on the inside
Short, sharp barrel section
Busy peak through the middle of the dry season
notes: A short, barrelling peak that is more forgiving on smaller swells than its neighbours, which is what makes it the Bukit break an intermediate can realistically surf. Best once the SE trades are established and the tide is right, through the middle of the dry season.

name: Impossibles
hazards: Shallow coral reef
Long paddle back after a completed wave
Exposed stretch of reef with little shelter
notes: One of the west-facing Bukit reefs that come into their own in the dry season, when the SE trades blow straight offshore. It sits on the same run of coast as Padang Padang and Bingin and shares their April to October window, strongest from June to August.

name: Balangan
hazards: Shallow coral reef
Reef shelf exposed on the lower tides
Current running down the reef on bigger swells
notes: The northern end of the Bukit's west-facing run of left-hand reefs, at its best across the dry season on SE trade winds. Part of the same April to October pattern as Uluwatu, Padang Padang, Bingin and Impossibles, with the mid-year months carrying the most size.

name: Keramas
hazards: Shallow volcanic rock bottom
Powerful, square barrel section
Wet-season run-off affecting water quality
notes: The reason Bali has no off season. When the wet season arrives and the wind switches to the NW, the Bukit shuts down and the east coast turns on. Keramas is the payoff: a right-hander over shallow volcanic rock that produces the most powerful barrels on the island, and it rewards advanced surfers only. Best at mid tide, November to March.

name: Chaweng Beach
hazards: Long flat spells outside the NE monsoon window
Swimmers and beachfront boat traffic
Waves rarely exceed 1 to 1.5 metres, so board choice decides whether you surf or float

sections.name: Southern end
sections.notes: One of the two stretches of the bay that hold the best shape once the NE monsoon is running.

sections.name: Central Chaweng
sections.notes: The other reliable stretch, and where the long left-hander sets up at mid to high tide.

notes: Ko Samui's primary spot, and the clearest expression of why this island is on the list: it works when the Bukit does not. The NE monsoon blows offshore from November and cleans up the wind swell generated through the October to December wet season, producing a long left-hander at mid to high tide that is made for a longboard or a SUP. The southern and central ends of the bay are the parts worth walking to.

name: Lamai Beach
hazards: Small and inconsistent for most of the year
Swimmers along a busy resort beach
notes: The smaller, cleaner alternative to Chaweng, and the better call on the days when the surf is small, which on this coast is most of them. A genuine beginner's beach break on sand taking both lefts and rights, running on the same NE monsoon window of November to February.

name: Lances Right
hazards: Shallow, sharp reef; booties are standard
The barrel runs over the shallowest part of the reef
Remote: the nearest medical help is a boat ride away

sections.name: The Office
sections.notes: The fast section, where the wave runs away from you and asks for commitment.

sections.name: The Main Peak
sections.notes: Walls over the shallow reef that earned the nickname the surgeon's table.

notes: World-class barrels, and the wave the Mentawai charter fleet is built around. Prime through the dry season from March to November, when the winds are favourable and the swell arrives consistently large.

name: Macaronis
hazards: Shallow, sharp reef; booties are standard
The most crowded wave in the chain
Remote: the nearest medical help is a boat ride away
notes: The most ripable wave in the chain and the one that makes the Mentawais legible to an intermediate. A mechanical left-hander that repeats the same shape set after set, workable on the smaller days. It is also the break here that reliably gets crowded.

name: Lances Left
hazards: Shallow, sharp reef; booties are standard
Hollow sections between the open walls
Remote: the nearest medical help is a boat ride away
notes: Consistent, fun, rippable walls with hollow sections mixed through them. It sits across from Lances Right and gives the same anchorage a second option, which is why a charter can hold position here for days. Prime March to November.

name: Rifles
hazards: Shallow, sharp reef; booties are standard
Heavy, critical take-off with no margin
Remote: the nearest medical help is a boat ride away
notes: Heavy, critical and fast. An expert-only right-hander that gives nothing back for a late take-off, and one of the reasons the chain has the reputation it does. Prime through the dry season, March to November.

name: Greenbush
hazards: Shallow, sharp reef; booties are standard
Heavy barrel with a thick lip
Remote: the nearest medical help is a boat ride away
notes: A heavy barrel and expert territory in every condition it breaks in. It is the wave people book the trip for and then watch from the boat. Prime March to November.

name: Bankvaults
hazards: Shallow, sharp reef; booties are standard
Critical section over the shallowest reef
Remote: the nearest medical help is a boat ride away
notes: A critical reef break, and a right-hander in a chain celebrated for its lefts. Advanced and above, prime through the dry season from March to November.
